title: Reading garden — contextual bridges & practical takeaways
content:
Reading garden: quick pass on 'contextual bridges' ideas and follow-ups

Purpose: informal capture of papers/blogs/talks that feel relevant to long-context serving. Mostly: how to stitch discontiguous context, KV-cache policies, and cheap proxies for quality when trimming history.

High-level notes (raw):
- Term I'm using here: 'contextual bridge' = lightweight auxiliary state that helps the model recall or re-locate content from far history without materializing all tokens in the active window. Examples: compact summaries, anchors, link-indexed KV slots.
- Why it matters for Redwood: we can reduce per-token cost (and memory pressure) if cheap bridges preserve downstream answer quality for common QA/dialog tasks. Also fits Dedicated and Private constraints where memory per-server is a hard limit.

Papers / items skimmed (my quick take):
1) "Fragment Matching for Long-Context LLMs" (arXiv 2309.xxxx) — TL;DR: index fragments with vector keys + a lightweight match-and-concat scheme.
   - Idea: maintain a short retrieval index of salient fragments, on each request match top-k and append compressed fragment summaries instead of full history.
   - Pros: straightforward, works with off-the-shelf models. Cons: risk of mismatched grounding (introduces hallucinated 'context' if matches are imprecise).
   - Notes: they use chunk-wise embeddings with L2 rerank; interesting that rerank is cheap compared to full generation.
   - Redwood experiments to try: simulate fragment matching + Redwood's KV prefix caching (how does matching behave when internal KV is warm vs cold?). Metric: answer exactness / F1 on QA set vs latency and token-cost.

2) "Sparse KV Eviction Patterns" blog (internal/linked above) — TL;DR: heuristics for evicting KV cache entries while preserving reply quality.
   - Key heuristics: age-weighted importance, topic-entropy proxy (higher entropy = keep), ephemeral tokens (timestamps, ephemeral outputs) flagged for early eviction.
   - Practical: cheapest to compute on request router rather than inside runtime; we can tag tokens at generation time.
   - Experiment: implement age+topic heuristic in a lightweight router filter and compare to LRU baseline for a conversational workload.

3) Streaming-attention talk (MLConf) — TL;DR: reduce compute for prefix attention by quantizing attention keys and using block-wise attention for far-prefix tokens.
   - Implementation nuance: works best if far-prefix interactions are mostly topic-level, not token-level exact matches.
   - On Redwood: this may allow longer effective context on the same hardware if we accept slight quality drop for very far tokens. Worth quantifying with small AB tests.

4) "Prompt condensation" (small workshop paper) — TL;DR: use a tiny model to produce a condensed natural language summary of a long context window; feed condensed summary + recent context into main model.
   - Tradeoffs: extra model latency + potential compression loss. But if condensation model is tiny (distilled), overall cost may still be lower than re-sending full history.

Open hypotheses / questions:
- H1: For multi-turn help desks, 70% of lost context utility can be recovered using a 1–3 sentence natural-language bridge per 1k tokens removed.
- H2: Topic-level anchors (keyword + embedding) + one-sentence reconstructor beats naive fragment matching when user queries require paraphrase-level retrieval.
- Q: Which proxy metric best predicts downstream QA drop after eviction? Candidate proxies: embedding-sim drop, LM perplexity delta when conditioning on condensed vs full context, and rerank score gap. Need to validate.

Concrete experiment plan (lean MVP):
- Dataset: internal support-chat dump (anonymized) + SQuAD-style synthetic QA from long docs. Pick ~5k dialogs with average 6–20 turns.
- Models: 1) baseline: small open model (Redwood-verified 7B) with full last-16k tokens. 2) condensed-bridge pipeline: tiny condenser (300M) -> 7B main with last 2k tokens + 1–3 sentence bridge. 3) fragment-match pipeline: top-3 fragments appended. 4) router-evict LRU vs age+entropy.
- Metrics: answer F1/EM, Rouge-L of generated summaries when ground-truth synopsis available, latency p50/p95, token-cost per request. Secondary: failure modes count (hallucinations, contradictions).
- Run plan: start with offline synthetic QA (cheap to label), then small live rollout behind a canary route on Redwood Dedicated with traffic throttled.

Quick implementation notes (what blocks I expect):
- Need a cheap condenser model and training data. Could finetune on chat->1–2 sentence pairs derived from the logs (extractive heuristics + human checks).
- Integrate bridge insertion at the router layer so we can A/B without touching runtime kernel. This is important for Dedicated and Private.
- Instrumentation: capture a compact 'delta' telemetry: tokens avoided, predicted quality proxy, actual quality delta on sampled requests. Add a flag in trace span for whether bridge was used.

Action items / TODOs (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] @Maya Chen: run embedding-sim gap experiment for fragment vs condensed summary on 500 dialogs (deadline: 2026-06-24). Link results to INF-4218.
- [ ] @Owen Brooks: prototype router hook that can call condenser and annotate a request with 'bridge' text instead of extending token buffer (deadline: 2026-06-28).
- [ ] Julian (me): draft evaluation harness + metrics dashboard template (p50/95 latency, EM/F1, token-cost), push to github repo context-bridge-exps.

Notes-to-self (bits & pieces):
- Slack threads: #eng-inference/context-ops has an ongoing convo about eviction tags — ping @ops for cost numbers.
- Quick caution: condensed text is human-readable and may leak PII if used naively; ensure condenser has PII scrub step or run only on anonymized corpora for experiments.
- If condenser is tiny and cheap, we might run it in the router (<50ms added) — measure on Dedicated GPU vs CPU.

Brainstorm: 'anchor-routing' experiment idea
- Maintain an index of anchors per user (1–5 phrase anchors). On each turn, match query to top anchor; if anchor similarity high, send anchor + recent window otherwise send full window. Anchors updated every N turns or when similarity drift detected. This could be a hybrid between condense and fragment-match.

References / reading log (to re-open later):
- FragMatch paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.01234 (skim)
- Sparse KV eviction blog / internal: https://blog.redwood.ai/context-eviction-patterns
- Streaming attention notes from MLConf 2026 (video link internal)
- Prompt condensation workshop paper (pdf attached in drive?)

End of notes. Feel free to steal, comment, or re-organize for a proper RFC if we get promising early results.

-- Julian
